# Cahn–Hilliard spinodal decomposition {#sec-cahn-hilliard}

`apps/cahn_hilliard` — conserved fourth-order phase separation, parameterised
for the Fe–Cr miscibility gap.

## Physical setting

An Fe–Cr alloy held at 475 °C inside its chemical spinodal separates
spontaneously into Fe-rich and Cr-rich domains. There is no nucleation barrier:
every long-wavelength composition fluctuation grows. The technological interest
is that this is the mechanism behind "475 °C embrittlement" in ferritic
stainless steels, and the length scale of the resulting microstructure sets the
mechanical consequence.

The question the science presets ask is therefore quantitative: **how does the
$\alpha/\alpha'$ domain size evolve from early band selection through
late-stage coarsening, and at what rate?** The named observable is the
**characteristic domain length $L(t) = 2\pi/k_1$**, where $k_1$ is the first
moment of the azimuthally averaged structure factor, together with its growth
exponent. Two supporting observables come out of the same diagnostics: the
**selected wave number $k_{\mathrm{peak}}$** at early times, which linear
theory predicts, and the mean composition, which must not move at all.

## Problem setup

This application ships both kinds of preset and the difference matters. The
**verification presets** are `fe_cr_spinodal.json` — a single Fourier mode
whose growth rate is known in closed form — and `coarsening.json`, a broadband
illustrative case. Both use the older regular-solution free energy with
$\Omega = 20.1\,\mathrm{kJ\,mol^{-1}}$ at $c_0 = 0.32$ and grid-unit $\kappa$
and $M$: they are **not calibrated Fe–Cr timescales and not production science
cases**. The **science presets** are `fe_cr_early_stage.json` and the two
`fe_cr_coarsening` files, which use the assessed Redlich–Kister
[@Redlich1948] thermodynamics
and carry a code-to-physical scale map. The table describes the science
presets.

| Item | Description |
|---|---|
| Use case | Thermal ageing of a ferritic Fe–Cr alloy inside the 475 °C miscibility gap — the mechanism behind "475 °C embrittlement" |
| Domain | 2-D periodic representative volume: $256^2$ (early stage) or $512^2$ (coarsening) cells at $\Delta x = 1$ code unit $= 1.068\ \mathrm{nm}$, i.e. 273 nm and 547 nm per side |
| Grid | Early stage: $t \in [0, 400]$ at $\Delta t = 0.5$, sampled every 20. Coarsening: $t \in [0, 4000]$ at $\Delta t = 0.5$, sampled every 100 — about 1114 h of ageing at 475 °C, since one code time unit is $1003\ \mathrm{s} = 0.278\ \mathrm{h}$ at $c_0 = 0.5$ |
| Boundary conditions | Periodic on both active axes |
| Initial condition | `seeded_noise`: deterministic hashed noise bounded by $\pm 0.005$ about the mean Cr fraction, with the global mean removed by an exact integer reduction, so the initial field is identical on any number of MPI ranks |
| Key physical parameters | $T = 748.15\ \mathrm{K}$ (475 °C); Redlich–Kister $L_0 = 20500 - 9.68\,T\ \mathrm{J\,mol^{-1}}$, $L_1 = 0$; $V_m = 7.09\times10^{-6}\ \mathrm{m^3\,mol^{-1}}$; $\kappa = 10^{-9}\ \mathrm{J\,m^{-1}}$; $D = D_0e^{-Q/RT}$ with $D_0 = 2\times10^{-5}\ \mathrm{m^2\,s^{-1}}$ and $Q = 241\ \mathrm{kJ\,mol^{-1}}$. Compositions $c_0 = 0.50$ and $c_0 = 0.45$ |
| Observable | Domain length $L(t) = 2\pi/k_1$ and its growth exponent; early-stage $k_{\mathrm{peak}}$; mean composition (conserved); total free energy (must decrease) |
| Model maturity | numerical verification: **analytical** — the linear growth rate, the $L(k)$ symbol, the gradient energy and a synthetic power-law fit are all checked against closed forms · physical completeness: **reduced** without elasticity (no magnetic contribution to the bcc Gibbs energy); **extended** by `cahn_hilliard_elastic`, which adds a Vegard eigenstrain on the existing Green operator · calibration: **representative**. The interaction parameter is the classical bcc Cr–Fe assessment of @Andersson1987, but the application states plainly that its thermodynamic and kinetic constants are *"representative, not verified against the primary sources digit by digit"*. Treat the numbers as semi-quantitative |

A periodic cell represents an interior volume of bulk material far from any
free surface or grain boundary. That is the right idealisation for spinodal
decomposition specifically, because it is a bulk instability with no nucleation
barrier and no preferred site — there is nothing for a surface to do here that
the bulk is not already doing everywhere. What it excludes is exactly what its
name implies: free surfaces, grain boundaries, and any long-range stress field
that could couple to composition. Coherent elastic misfit in particular is
known to bias $\alpha/\alpha'$ morphology and is **not** in this model. The box
must also be large compared with the selected wavelength, or the structure
factor is measuring the box rather than the alloy: at $c_0 = 0.5$ the model
predicts $\lambda_{\max} \approx 17.3$ code units, so $512^2$ holds about 30
wavelengths per side.

### One consequence worth knowing

With the assessed Redlich–Kister interaction, Fe–32Cr at 475 °C is **outside**
the spinodal — it sits in the nucleation-and-growth regime, where this model
does not apply. The older representative $\Omega = 20.1\ \mathrm{kJ\,mol^{-1}}$
is deeper and does place it inside, which is why the verification presets can
keep using $c_0 = 0.32$ while the science presets moved to $c_0 = 0.45$ and
$c_0 = 0.50$. The model computes its own spinodal band for whatever
coefficients it is given, and a test asserts this.

### Measured

| Quantity | Predicted | Measured |
|---|---|---|
| Early-stage fastest-growing wave number | $k_{\max} = 0.3624$ | $k_{\mathrm{peak}} = 0.3682$, within one shell |
| Coarsening exponent $n$ in $L \propto t^{n}$, $c_0 = 0.50$, fitted over $t \in [2000, 4000]$ | $1/3$ (Lifshitz–Slyozov) | $0.353$, reaching $L = 39.8\ \mathrm{nm}$ after 1114 h |
| Coarsening exponent, $c_0 = 0.45$ | $1/3$ | $0.371$, reaching $36.6\ \mathrm{nm}$ after 943 h |
| Mean Cr fraction drift | $0$ | $2.1\times10^{-15}$ |

The fitting window is stated rather than hidden: over the whole run the
exponent drops to $0.31$, because the early interval is still wavelength
selection rather than coarsening.

## Governing equations

One conserved composition field $c$ (Cr mole fraction):

$$
\partial_t c \;=\; M\nabla^2\!\left( f'(c) - \kappa\nabla^2 c \right),
$$ {#eq-ch-pde}

with the regular-solution bulk free energy in units of $RT$,

$$
f(c) \;=\; \omega\,c(1-c) \;+\; c\ln c \;+\; (1-c)\ln(1-c),
\qquad \omega = \frac{\Omega}{RT}.
$$ {#eq-ch-f}

The excess term is a Redlich–Kister expansion in the general case,

$$
f_{\mathrm{ex}}(c) \;=\; \frac{c(1-c)}{RT}\sum_{i\ge 0} L_i\,(2c-1)^i ,
\qquad L_i = L_{i,a} + L_{i,b}\,T ,
$$ {#eq-ch-rk}

of which @eq-ch-f is the $L_0 = \Omega$, $L_{i>0} = 0$ special case — the same
expression, not a second code path, and a test asserts the reduction. The
science presets use the assessed bcc Cr–Fe interaction
$L_0 = 20500 - 9.68\,T\ \mathrm{J\,mol^{-1}}$ with $L_1 = 0$ [@Andersson1987]; the verification presets use the
older representative $\Omega = 20.1\,\mathrm{kJ\,mol^{-1}}$ at
$T = 748.15\,\mathrm{K}$, which is deeper and keeps Fe–32Cr inside the
spinodal.

Neither is a CALPHAD assessment carried out here. The coefficients are
representative and have not been verified against the primary sources digit by
digit, the magnetic contribution to the bcc Gibbs energy is omitted, and the
report does not claim quantitative agreement with a thermodynamic database.
Every constant is a JSON parameter precisely so a better assessment can be
substituted without touching code.

## Spectral formulation

Linearising the bulk term about the alloy composition $c_0$ puts $f''(c_0)$
into the linear symbol and leaves the remainder to the nonlinearity. With
$u = k_{\mathrm{lap}}$,

$$
L(k) \;=\; M\big( f''(c_0)\,u \;-\; \kappa\,u^2 \big),
\qquad
M_{\mathrm{nl}}(k) \;=\; M\,u ,
$$ {#eq-ch-symbol}

$$
N(c) \;=\; f'(c) - f'(c_0) - f''(c_0)\,(c-c_0).
$$ {#eq-ch-nl}

Both channels carry the factor $u$, so the mean composition is conserved
exactly.

The growth rate follows directly from @eq-ch-symbol. Writing
$|\mathbf{k}| = k$,

$$
\lambda(k) \;=\; -M k^2\big( f''(c_0) + \kappa k^2 \big),
$$ {#eq-ch-growth}

which is positive — unstable — precisely when $f''(c_0) < 0$, the spinodal
condition. The fastest-growing mode is at
$k_{\max}^2 = -f''(c_0)/(2\kappa)$, and this wavelength is what sets the
initial domain spacing.

The nonlinearity @eq-ch-nl is not a low-order polynomial — it contains
$\ln\!\big(c/(1-c)\big)$ — so dealiasing is on.

## Solution strategy

ETD1 as in @eq-etd1. Composition is clamped away from $\{0,1\}$ so the
logarithms stay finite; a sampled composition outside the physical range stops
the run rather than producing quiet nonsense.

Optional collective CSV diagnostics record mass, composition bounds, and the
current-state total energy including the spectral gradient contribution.

## Verification

* **Analytical growth rate.** A single seeded mode grows as
  $e^{\lambda(k)t}$ with $\lambda$ from @eq-ch-growth, matched within 5%.
* **Mass conservation.** The mean composition is held to $10^{-12}$ across a
  run.
* **Free energy decreases.** The total free energy falls monotonically while a
  spinodal mode grows.
* **Gradient energy.** The diagnostic gradient energy matches the analytical
  value on distributed grids.
* **Decomposition independence.** Seeded noise produces the same field and the
  same mean on any number of ranks.
* **Redlich–Kister reduction.** With $L_1 = 0$ the expansion reproduces the
  regular-solution expressions exactly, and its first and second derivatives
  match finite differences.
* **Spinodal band.** The computed band agrees with the closed-form roots when
  $L_1 = 0$, and a shallow interaction is correctly reported as having no
  miscibility gap.
* **Physical scales.** The code-to-physical length and time conversion is
  checked against its closed form, with a sanity bound that caught an incorrect
  first derivation.
* **Structure factor.** The diagnostic recovers the wave number of a single
  known mode, and the exponent fit recovers $1/3$ exactly from a synthetic
  $L \propto t^{1/3}$ series.
* **Coherent elasticity.** A uniform composition under a uniform Vegard
  eigenstrain does not move ($\nabla^2\mu_{\mathrm{el}}=0$). Mass is
  conserved on a noisy $32^2$ cell with cubic $C_{ij}$. The Green operator
  itself is the dendrite/inverse suite in `test_microelasticity.cpp`.

## Binaries and inputs

`cahn_hilliard` (CPU), `cahn_hilliard_hip`, `cahn_hilliard_elastic` (CPU,
Vegard Green-operator coupling; host-only, #157). Presets:
`fe_cr_spinodal.json` (single-mode verification), `coarsening.json`
(seeded broadband), `fe_cr_elastic.json` (coherent cubic misfit).

## Visualisation

@fig-ch-spinodal is the science cell: $512\times 512$ of Fe–50Cr at 475 °C, late
enough that the binodals have been reached and the labyrinth has
coarsened. HIP job 21968070, preset `fe_cr_coarsening.json`, $t=4000$
($\approx 1114$ h). The colour scale is diverging and centred on $c_0=0.5$.
One code cell is $1.068\,\mathrm{nm}$, so the box is $547\,\mathrm{nm}$ on
a side.

![Cahn–Hilliard spinodal at $512\times 512$, $c_0=0.5$, $t=4000$. Bicontinuous
$\alpha/\alpha'$ labyrinth after 1114 h of ageing at 475 °C. HIP job
21968070, `fe_cr_coarsening.json`.](figures/cahn_hilliard_spinodal_512.png){#fig-ch-spinodal}

That labyrinth is the *incoherent* morphology: no misfit, no preferred
direction. A coherent $\alpha/\alpha'$ pair carries a Vegard eigenstrain
$\varepsilon^{*}=\varepsilon_0(c-c_{\mathrm{ref}})I$. @fig-ch-elastic is
the same conserved Cahn–Hilliard and the same Green operator as the
dendrite, four ways (job 21969396, $256^2$ unless noted):

- no misfit — isotropic labyrinth ($512^2$, job 21968070);
- isotropic Vegard, $\varepsilon_0=0.04$ — still a labyrinth, slightly
  coarser (2-D $Y(\mathbf n)$ is not flat, axis power $0.60$);
- cubic Fe-like $C_{ij}$, $\varepsilon_0=0.04$ — $\langle 100\rangle$
  bands, axis power $0.96$ at $t=40$;
- cubic $\varepsilon_0=0.08$ — $2Y\varepsilon_0^2$ beats $|f''|$, the
  spinodal is dead (amplitude $8\times 10^{-5}$).

$\varepsilon_0=0.04$ is illustrative, not a fitted $da/dc$. The magnetic
Gibbs-energy term is still absent; the device Green is still #157.

![Four coherent-spinodal outcomes. Top left: no misfit. Top right:
isotropic Vegard. Bottom left: cubic Vegard, $\langle 100\rangle$
aligned. Bottom right: cubic Vegard large enough to suppress the
instability. Job 21969396.](figures/cahn_hilliard_elastic_quartet.png){#fig-ch-elastic}

{{< pagebreak >}}

![Cubic Vegard Cahn–Hilliard, $512\times 512$, $t=40$. Axis power $0.955$,
$c\in[0.073,0.930]$. Job 21969476.](figures/cahn_hilliard_elastic_aligned.png){#fig-ch-elastic-aligned}

The aligned state also coarsens, still on the axes: @fig-ch-elastic-pair
is $t=20$ (axis power $0.975$) against $t=40$.

![Same cubic run, $t=20$ vs $t=40$. The Manhattan labyrinth thickens;
it does not relax back to an isotropic one.](figures/cahn_hilliard_elastic_pair.png){#fig-ch-elastic-pair}

Coarsening is the result that a time strip of similar-looking fields
cannot show. @fig-ch-coarsening is the same run at $t=400$ (wavelength
already selected, $L\approx 17.7$ cells) and $t=4000$ ($L\approx 37.3$
cells $= 39.8\,\mathrm{nm}$). Shared colour scale: the domains thicken,
the topology stays bicontinuous, the mean composition does not move.

![Same $512\times 512$ Fe–50Cr run, $t=400$ vs $t=4000$. Domain length doubles;
the colour scale is shared.](figures/cahn_hilliard_coarsening_pair.png){#fig-ch-coarsening}

{{< pagebreak >}}

The initial condition, not the equation, decides the micrograph.
@fig-ch-comparison is the verification thermodynamics ($\Omega = 20.1\,\mathrm{kJ\,mol^{-1}}$,
$c_0=0.32$) at $512\times 512$ and $t=10$: one Fourier mode near $k_{\max}$
(@eq-ch-growth) stays a stripe; broadband noise has already broken into
Cr-rich droplets. $t=10$ is the latest sample that is still physically
sane for the single-mode seed — past $t\approx 12$ that run overshoots
$c\in[0,1]$ (ETD1 is not unconditionally stable at large amplitude).

![Same alloy, same $t=10$, $512\times 512$ cell, central $192\times 192$ window:
single-mode seed vs broadband noise. The initial condition sets the
morphology.](figures/cahn_hilliard_comparison.png){#fig-ch-comparison}
